$comment: The black-and-gold colour system, and the single upstream every stella-facing
surface generates from. Normative definition: SPEC-stella-tui-v2.md sections 2-4.
Do not hand-edit a generated artifact. Edit this file, run `make tokens-update`,
and commit the regenerated files alongside it. `make tokens` fails the gate when
a generated file has drifted from this one, which is the mechanism replacing the
prose promise that four surfaces had been copying by hand.
Every token declares a `clamp` role. The role decides which predicate the value
is held to, so a new hex cannot enter the palette without a human choosing the
kind of colour it is -- and the warm-drift predicates reject the choice that
kills a gold-on-black scheme. The predicates are defined once in
crates/stella-tui-theme/src/clamp.rs and mirrored by scripts/check-tokens.py;
both are held to this file's `clamps` block below.
name: stella black and gold

reason: Bronze Gold #C58A32 is r=197 g=138 b=50. The resting-gold clamp requires
g >= 0.78 r, i.e. g >= 154. At 138 it fails by 16 points, which places it
in exactly the orange band SPEC 3.2 names as the failure mode: orange on a
near-black ground reads brown on uncalibrated panels. v4.0's own ground
#070B10 is r=7 g=11 b=16, which fails the neutral-gray predicate's r == g
in the green-tipped direction. The kit is superseded rather than tuned
because both of its anchor values are outside the clamp this system is

resting-gold.why: The green ratio is the load-bearing half: below it the hue is orange, and orange on a near-black ground reads brown on cheap panels.

gold-lift.predicate: r > g > b AND 100*g >= 78*r AND hue within 3 deg of `anchor` AND lighter than `anchor`
why: A lift is anchored to the gold it lifts, never held to a second blue
ceiling. An earlier revision of this file carried `lifted-gold` with
blue_pct 44 -- a bound reverse-engineered from the one token it had to
admit, which can say no to nothing in principle. It was answering the
wrong question: in a gold, lightness is (r + b) / 510, so the resting
ceiling 100*b <= 35*r caps lightness at (255 + 89) / 510 = 0.6745 for
ANY colour, and gold_bright sits at 0.6941. Above that line the resting
ceiling is not strict, it is unsatisfiable -- so a lift could never have
been held to it, and a looser ceiling repeats the category error one
notch down.
So the two clauses are stated where each is coherent. `100*g >= 78*r` is
the HUE rule -- gold versus orange, the argument SPEC 3.2 actually makes
-- and it holds at every lightness, so every gold carries it. The blue
ceiling is the SATURATION rule and governs only the resting gold, which
is not lightened. A lift is then pinned to the anchor: same hue within
hue_tolerance_deg, strictly lighter.
An anchor is the stronger constraint, not the looser one. A ceiling
admits every colour beneath it and keeps passing after the gold it was
cut for is gone; an anchor admits only the authored gold, brighter.
Recolour `gold` and leave `gold-bright` behind and the check fails,
naming the hue distance.
hue_tolerance_deg is derived, not chosen: stella-tui's v1 theme records
that its warning amber sits 4.0 deg from gold 'so an outcome may never
be told from chrome by hue alone'. 4 deg is the distance this repository
already treats as indistinguishable, so a lift -- which must be the SAME
hue -- sits inside it.
SPEC 3.2's gray clamp is stated for the neutral ramp, and the two
silvers do not satisfy its r == g half by design -- they sit one to two
points off neutral, which is the tilt SPEC 3.1's opening sentence
describes. Left unclamped they would be the palette's one unguarded
warm-drift surface, the metal that appears on every read, skill and
memory row, so they carry the weaker predicate that still forbids the
failure mode: blue strictly above red, green never below it.

neutral-gray.why: Neutral, or tipped toward blue; never toward red. A gray one point warm is what makes a black-and-gold scheme read as sepia. Scoped to the deck's near-black ground; the light ramp carries `warm-paper`.

warm-paper.why: The light ground's clamp: warm or neutral, never blue. The floors keep paper from becoming tan, and are taken from brand v1.0's own light neutrals, which sit at g = 0.988 r and b = 0.960 r.

verdict.why: Green and red are deliberately neither metal nor gray. SPEC 2 asks for them desaturated and cool; that is a review judgement, not a channel predicate, so no predicate is asserted rather than a decorative one being invented.

surface.why: Diff row backgrounds are tints carrying a sign column, not hues in a role. They are held by the diff renderer's contract (the + and - signs are mandatory), not by a channel test.

$comment: Web-only stops. Every token below carries no `rust` name, because the
terminal never draws it and every entry in the generated `ALL` table
needs a 256-colour fallback -- an ANSI approximation of a paper tint
would be an assertion about nothing. `scripts/gen-tokens.py` skips
them, so `crates/stella-tui-theme/src/generated.rs` is unchanged.
They are declared here rather than left in the site's stylesheet
because that is what puts them under a clamp. Until now the only file
that knew the site's warning hue was the site, and the 30-degree
separation law that governs it on the terminal was, on the web, a
sentence in a comment (#4071). The light ramp is the one #4072 records
as derived rather than specified; specifying it here is what closes
that gap.
The values themselves are unchanged -- these are the stops the site
already ships, moved under the system rather than re-cut.
